utility.notes: Emeryville is a well-documented Alameda County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: Ava Community Energy
value.notes: Ava Community Energy (formerly East Bay Community Energy) confirms Emeryville as a current member city, alongside Albany, Berkeley, Dublin, Fremont, Hayward, Livermore, Newark, Oakland, Piedmont, Pleasanton, San Leandro, and Union City in Alameda County. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Emeryville/Alameda County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value: Request the inspection via the Inspection Request Line (510) 596-4315 the day before, no later than 6:00 a.m. the morning of the requested date
Verify the work to be inspected is complete and ready, and have the Contractor present at the time of inspection
Leave a callback phone number; inspection staff will notify the contact if the time frame changes
Provide a ladder for access as needed for the Building Inspector
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division construction/inspection process (the same document covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: Search-engine synthesis indicates a typical approval time of 3 business days for the Symbium-based online permitting platform; not independently confirmed via direct fetch this session.

other_conditions: Larger rooftop solar systems (10kW and above) require standard building and electrical permits with plan review; a PE stamp is typically required for systems over 10kW

permit_fees.notes: A third-party guide cites $250-$500 for Emeryville solar permits, but this was not independently confirmed against the city's own fee schedule this session.
